heard: A four-kilometer mountain swept past Earth while tumbling completely out of control. On September 29, 2004, the asteroid Tautates made a startlingly close approach. It swept within four lunar distances, or roughly 1.5 million kilometers of Earth. Measuring roughly 4.5 kilometers in length, it was the closest flyby of its size this century. Online chain emails predicted doom, but radar dishes at Goldstone and Arecibo mapped its true face. Tautates was a contact binary of two distinct lobes, shaped remarkably like a ginger root. Stranger still, it never spins cleanly, tumbling through space like a flubbed pass across two independent cycles. Calculations prove Earth is safe for at least six centuries from that chaotic wanderer.
